input.title: Archive a book
input.description: A librarian can archive a book record. Archived records remain available to librarians and are excluded from public search.
input.project_context: A library catalogue serves librarians and public readers.

ambiguity_issues: The mechanism or trigger for public search exclusion is not specified beyond stating the exclusion rule.
missing_information: The specific system interface or action name required for a librarian to perform the archival action is not defined.
The definition of what constitutes public search versus librarian availability is missing implementation details.
clarification_questions: What specific action or interface element triggers the archiving of a book record by a librarian?
How should the system verify that a book record is excluded from public search?
testability_issues: Testing public search exclusion depends on how public search is implemented, which is currently unstated.
edge_cases: Attempting to archive a book record that is already archived.
Attempting to archive a book record while lacking librarian permissions.
acceptance_criteria: When a librarian initiates the archiving of a book record, the record state updates to archived.
Archived book records remain accessible to librarians.
Archived book records are excluded from public search results.
risk_reasons: Risk is Medium because ambiguity regarding search exclusion mechanisms may lead to public exposure of archived records depending on implementation.
priority_reasons: Priority is Medium as specified by the input data, but the business rationale needs stakeholder confirmation since none was supplied.
analysis.improved_requirement: A librarian can archive a book record such that archived records remain available to librarians and are excluded from public search.
analysis.type_explanation: The requirement specifies system behaviors and actor permissions associated with modifying and filtering data records, which defines system functionality.

test_scenarios.title: Librarian archives a book record successfully
preconditions: The user is authenticated as a librarian.
An active book record exists in the system.
test_steps: The librarian requests archiving for the book record.
test_scenarios.expected_result: The book record is successfully archived, remains accessible to librarians, and does not appear in public search results.

test_scenarios.title: Non-librarian attempts to archive a book record
preconditions: The user is not authenticated as a librarian.
An active book record exists in the system.
test_steps: The user attempts to request archiving for the book record.
test_scenarios.expected_result: The archival action is denied based on permissions.

input.title: Transfer notifications
input.description: Send an email for every approved transfer. Never send email for approved transfers.
input.project_context: Both notification statements have equal authority and no precedence decision exists.

ambiguity_issues: The requirement contains directly contradictory instructions regarding whether to send an email for approved transfers.
conflict_issues: Statement 1 requires sending an email for every approved transfer, while Statement 2 states never to send an email for approved transfers, and no precedence decision exists.
missing_information: Unresolved decision on whether approved transfers should trigger email notifications or not.
clarification_questions: Should approved transfers trigger an email notification or should they never trigger an email notification?
testability_issues: The requirement cannot be tested because it contains mutually exclusive outcomes for the exact same condition.
edge_cases: BLOCKED pending clarification: Behavior when a transfer is approved.
acceptance_criteria: BLOCKED pending clarification: AC-001 depends on the resolution of [TO BE CONFIRMED: whether approved transfers send an email or never send an email]. If sending is chosen, an email is sent for every approved transfer. If not sending is chosen, no email is sent for any approved transfer.
risk_reasons: The risk level is High because the direct contradiction makes implementation impossible to validate and creates uncertainty in core system behavior.
priority_reasons: The priority is Medium as specified in the input data, but no business rationale is supplied, requiring stakeholder confirmation.
analysis.improved_requirement: Send an email for every approved transfer [TO BE CONFIRMED: or never send an email for approved transfers].
analysis.type_explanation: The requirement specifies system behavior regarding automated email generation based on a transfer status change, which is a functional capability.

input.title: View own support tickets
input.description: An authenticated customer can view only their own support tickets.
input.project_context: Authenticated customers own their own support tickets. Agent access is outside this requirement.

ambiguity_issues: The definition of how support tickets are associated with an authenticated customer is not specified.
missing_information: The exact attributes or details of a support ticket that must be displayed to the customer are not defined.
clarification_questions: What specific ticket details must be displayed when an authenticated customer views their support tickets?
testability_issues: Testing is limited because the required attributes and presentation format of the tickets are unspecified.
edge_cases: BLOCKED pending clarification: An authenticated customer with zero support tickets attempting to view tickets.
BLOCKED pending clarification: An authenticated customer attempting to view tickets belonging to another customer.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: An authenticated customer must be able to view their own support tickets.
AC-002: An authenticated customer must be restricted from viewing support tickets belonging to other customers.
risk_reasons: Risk is Medium because unauthorized data access or information disclosure could occur if ownership isolation is not properly enforced, though impact depends on the sensitivity of the ticket contents.
priority_reasons: Priority is Medium based on the input, but a business rationale needs stakeholder confirmation.
analysis.improved_requirement: An authenticated customer can view only their own support tickets [TO BE CONFIRMED: specifying exact ticket attributes to display and handling for zero tickets].
analysis.type_explanation: The requirement specifies system behavior related to user permissions and data retrieval for authenticated users.

test_scenarios.title: Authenticated customer views own support tickets
preconditions: User is authenticated as a customer.
test_scenarios.expected_result: Only tickets belonging to the authenticated customer are displayed.

test_scenarios.title: Authenticated customer attempts to view other customers tickets
preconditions: User is authenticated as Customer A.
Support tickets exist for Customer B.
test_steps: Request to view tickets belonging to Customer B.
test_scenarios.expected_result: Tickets belonging to Customer B are not displayed to Customer A.

input.title: Shipment status latency
input.description: Under 200 simultaneous authenticated users, 95% of shipment-status API responses must complete within 2 seconds during a 30-minute load test.
input.project_context: The measured endpoint returns shipment status to authenticated users.

ambiguity_issues: The requirement specifies a 30-minute load test and 200 simultaneous authenticated users, but it does not define the warm-up period, ramp-up time, or the distribution rate of requests during the test.
missing_information: Unspecified ramp-up time and request frequency per user during the load test.
Unspecified definition of what constitutes a completed shipment-status API response (e.g., HTTP status code or specific payload structure).
clarification_questions: What is the required ramp-up time for reaching the 200 simultaneous authenticated users?
What specific request rate or think-time per user should be maintained during the 30-minute load test?
What exact HTTP status codes and payload structures define a successful shipment-status API response?
testability_issues: The test lacks a defined ramp-up profile and request frequency, which makes exact test execution steps non-deterministic unless clarified.
edge_cases: BLOCKED pending clarification on request frequency and ramp-up behavior at the exact boundary of 200 simultaneous users.
acceptance_criteria: Under a load of 200 simultaneous authenticated users during a 30-minute test, 95% of shipment-status API responses must complete within 2 seconds.
BLOCKED pending clarification: AC-002 depends on the exact definition of a completed API response and load ramp-up profile.
risk_reasons: Risk is Medium because performance characteristics under load can fail unpredictably if infrastructure scaling or database bottlenecks are unaddressed, though impact is limited to API response latency rather than data loss.
priority_reasons: The priority is Medium as stated in the source data, but the business rationale needs stakeholder confirmation since none was supplied.
analysis.improved_requirement: During a 30-minute load test with 200 simultaneous authenticated users, 95% of shipment-status API responses must complete within 2 seconds [TO BE CONFIRMED: ramp-up profile, request frequency, and success criteria definition].
analysis.type_explanation: The requirement specifies measurable performance and latency thresholds under a specific load, which classifies it strictly as a Non-Functional requirement.

test_scenarios.title: Shipment status API latency within threshold under load
preconditions: The shipment-status API endpoint is accessible
test_steps: Execute the load test for 30 minutes with 200 simultaneous authenticated users
Measure the completion time of all shipment-status API responses
test_scenarios.expected_result: 95% of the shipment-status API responses complete within 2 seconds
